why: International development funder (125 grants through FY2025) with recurring grants for solar and clean water projects in Salvadoran and Nicaraguan villages (x5).
No grants in the last five years (latest FY2016), so only its name suggests water work.
9 of its 16 grants (through FY2025) fund wells and safe drinking water, e.g. in Uganda, via Drop in the Bucket, Splash and charity: water; preselected grantees only.
Gives token amounts (median $100, largest $1,250) to global health and cookstove groups, with no water grants shown.

Large grants (latest FY2024) for clean water, sanitation and hygiene to IRC International Water and Sanitation, WaterAid America and Catholic Relief Services, though only to preselected organizations.
Grants through FY2024 include clean water projects (x4) and $9.1M to Global Water Challenge, one of its largest recipients.
6 grants through FY2024 for hand pump repair in the Congo, rainwater harvesting at schools and water filters, mainly via Gravity Water.
30 grants through FY2025 to build water wells in Zambia, Malawi, Liberia, Guatemala, the Congo and other countries.
7 grants through FY2025 for clean water and hygiene education, mostly to DigDeep, with no developing-country water projects shown.
All 29 grants (through FY2024) fund clean water projects, e.g. via Water 1st International, Water Access Now and Etta Projects.
